steps: Check UT-AIR compressor telemetry including compressor_current_a, header_pressure_bar, and oil_temp_c: continuously high current and low header pressure would support a major plant air leak or compressor capacity failure, while normal cycling and pressure would refute a plant-wide utility supply issue.

Check ST20-WLD local pneumatic pressure (air_pressure_bar): pressure dropping below normal range (5.3 to 5.9 bar) while plant header pressure remains normal would support a localized hose rupture, valve leak, or regulator failure at weld cell A; normal station pressure would refute pneumatic starvation at ST20.

Assess whether air_pressure_bar on ST20-WLD is a sensor or data problem by comparing its signal characteristics (e.g., sudden drop to zero, step discontinuity, or telemetry dropout) against downstream station ST30-WLD air_pressure_bar: an isolated anomaly at ST20 without physical process disruption supports a transmitter or wiring fault rather than a genuine pneumatic loss.

Check upstream station ST10-PRS operation (cycle_time_s, hyd_pressure_bar, and motor_current_a): elevated cycle times or hydraulic loss would support an upstream mechanical stoppage starving ST20, whereas normal values would refute upstream line starvation.

Check ST20-WLD weld process tags (servo_temp_c, tip_resistance_mohm, and weld_current_ka): abnormal tip resistance or high servo temperatures would support tooling friction or weld gun mechanical binding, whereas nominal values would refute weld tooling failure.

citations.quote: When leakage plus demand exceed what the compressor can deliver, the compressor stays loaded, header pressure falls below the cut-in pressure, and the 5.6 bar low alarm (A-UTAIR-HDR-LO) follows.
A sustained fall in header pressure while the compressor runs loaded indicates demand exceeding supply, most often a distribution leak.

| Header pressure falling, compressor loaded continuously | Distribution leak (drop legs, couplings, hoses) or a new air user | Ultrasonic leak survey of the header and the ST20/ST30 drop legs with the cells stopped | Repair the leaks; confirm the header holds pressure (see Table 3-2) |
If the combined total of line leakage and weld cell demand exceeds compressor output capacity, the unit remains loaded continuously without reaching 7.3 bar.

citations.quote: Regulated gun air (`air_pressure_bar`) normally sits at 5.6 bar within 5.3 to 5.9 bar. Below 5 bar the cell raises a low-air alarm; at 4.6 bar the supply-air interlock stops the cell. Gun force alarms (A-ST20-GUN-FRC, A-ST30-GUN-FRC) can appear as the air falls.

When gun air pressure falls at ST20 and ST30 together, the cause is upstream in the plant air supply; check the header pressure (see Section 6.2 of AM-CA-01 (Plant Air System and Utilities)) before working on either cell.
When gun air falls at one cell only, check that cell's filter-regulator, drop-leg ball valve and quick couplings.

| Gun air low at one cell only | Filter-regulator element clogged, regulator drifted, or local leak | Read the cell gauge; listen for leaks at the drop leg and couplings | Replace the filter element; reset the regulator; repair the leak |

repair_steps: Perform ultrasonic leak survey along the compressed air header, drop legs, and flexible hoses to locate leaks.
Inspect quick-disconnect couplings and fittings around ST20-WLD drop leg for physical damage or loose connections.
Replace deteriorated hoses and leaking quick-connect couplings, applying thread sealant to threaded fittings.
Pressurize distribution header, verify system holds pressure, and confirm compressor returns to normal cycling.
